distribution: Arctic Cat dealerships worldwide, from June 2002 through December 2003, for between $6,500 and $8,500.

If this occurs, it could lead to a loss of control, that could result in severe injury or death.

Close the faucet. 2 - Turn the gas/temperature control knob clockwise to the maximum (VERY HOT) setting, and then slowly turn the knob back counterclockwise to the PILOT position, indicated by the yellow button. Listen for the main valve to close- this would be a popping or snapping sound. This sound is different from the clicking sound that the knob makes as you turn it. 3 - If you hear the popping sound then the valve is working properly. You should then read and follow the "Installation and Operating Instructions". If you do not hear the popping sound then do not attempt to light the pilot and replace the valve. 4 - If the unit has been stored or is being installed in a cold environment and the main valve does not close before the knob is turned back to the PILOT position, the gas control valve must be warmed up to a temperature above 32 degrees F or 0 degrees C. Once warmed up, repeat the procedure above. If the gas control valve does not close (popping sound), replace the valve. If the water is too hot or if the temperature and pressure valve opens, turn down the temperature using the temperature control. If the water remains too hot or the temperature and pressure relief valve continues to open, then replace the valve.
injuries: None reported in the United States. (In Canada, where 140,000 units were sold, there were 45 incidents reported, including 15 reports of minor burns).

title: CPSC, BRIO Corp. Announce Recall of Toy Trumpet

remedies: Consumers should take down the "Fun Buckets" immediately and return them to the store where purchased, for a refund or a credit toward another product.

title: CPSC, Fireworks of Alabama Announce Recall of Bamboo-Stick Sparklers

hazards: The sparklers' bamboo-stick handles can catch fire, burn and disintegrate and emit burning fragments during use. These sparklers present a fire hazard and a risk of burn injury.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these sparklers immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a full refund.
injuries: CPSC and Fireworks of Alabama have not received any reports of injuries associated with these bamboo stick sparklers. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injuries.

title: CPSC, Robert Bosch Tool Corp. Announce Recall of Skil® Warrior Drill Battery Chargers
reason: The transformer inside the charger can overheat. If this occurs, the charger housing can melt and deform, possibly igniting flammable materials near or on the charger.
firm: Robert Bosch Tool Corp., of Chicago, Ill.

hazards: The transformer inside the charger can overheat. If this occurs, the charger housing can melt and deform, possibly igniting flammable materials near or on the charger.
remedies: Consumers should unplug the charger immediately. Consumers will receive a $25.00 rebate towards the purchase of any Skil® power tool.
injuries: Robert Bosch Tool Corp. has received one report of a charger causing a fire that resulted in property damage, and 160 reports of chargers overheating.

title: CPSC, Young's J.K. Inc. Announce Recall of Novelty Lighters
reason: These lighters do not have child-resistant mechanisms, as required by federal law. Young children can ignite the lighters, presenting fire and burn hazards.
firm: Young's J.K. Inc., of Portland, Ore.
distribution: Gas stations, smoke shops, grocery, gift and liquor stores sold the lighters in Oregon and Southwest Washington, from 1996 through October 2001, for between $8 and $20.
hazards: These lighters do not have child-resistant mechanisms, as required by federal law. Young children can ignite the lighters, presenting fire and burn hazards.
remedies: Consumers should stop using the lighters immediately and return them to the store where purchased for a refund.
injuries: CPSC has received one report of a 2-year-old using one of these lighters to ignite an upholstered chair. The fire resulted in the death of his 6-year-old brother and permanent brain damage to the 2-year old.

title: CPSC, Toro Company Recall Z-100 Riding Mowers
reason: The engines for these products had fuel lines that were too long and could possibly droop and come in contact with moving parts, which can cut the fuel lines, resulting in fuel leakage.
firm: The Toro Company, of Bloomington, Minn.

hazards: The engines for these products had fuel lines that were too long and could possibly droop and come in contact with moving parts, which can cut the fuel lines, resulting in fuel leakage.
remedies: Consumers should stop using their lawn mowers until the fuel lines can be shortened. Registered owners should already have received a letter with enclosed instruction sheet and reply card for this modification. Contact Toro or a Toro dealer for a free repair.
injuries: Toro has received no reports of fuel leaks, fires or injuries.

title: CPSC, Exmark Recalls Lazer HP Riding Mowers

Registered owners should already have received a letter with enclosed instruction sheet and reply card for this modification. For a copy of an instruction sheet detailing the modification or for a free repair, contact your Exmark dealer or call Exmark. No parts are necessary for this modification.

title: CPSC, Kawasaki Motors Corp. U.S.A. Announce Recall of ATVs
reason: There is the potential for failure of a weld securing the tie-rod plate to the steering column. If the weld fails, the plate can become detached from the steering column, resulting in a loss of steering control.
firm: Kawasaki Motors Corp., U.S.A. (KMC) of Irvine, Calif.
distribution: Kawasaki dealers sold these ATVs nationwide, from August 2002 through January 2003, for about $1799.
hazards: There is the potential for failure of a weld securing the tie-rod plate to the steering column. If the weld fails, the plate can become detached from the steering column, resulting in a loss of steering control.
remedies: Consumers should contact their Kawasaki dealer to schedule an appointment to replace the steering column.

title: CPSC, UWATEC AG Announce Recall of 1995 Aladin Air X NitrOx Dive Computers
product: Aladin Air X NitrOx dive domputers
reason: Software in the dive computers may inaccurately calculate desaturation times, resulting in possible decompression sickness under aggressive dive conditions.
firm: UWATEC AG, of Hallwil, Switzerland

hazards: Software in the dive computers may inaccurately calculate desaturation times, resulting in possible decompression sickness under aggressive dive conditions.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these dive computers immediately and contact UWATEC for a free replacement. Consumers will receive the current model, Aladin Air Z NitrOx.
injuries: UWATEC AG has received five reports of decompression sickness allegedly associated with the use of the 1995 dive computers.

title: CPSC, Trak Inc. Announce Recall of Snowshoe Bindings
product: Karhu Meta Sweeper and "Karhu Morph Sweeper" snowshoe bindings
reason: Screws and other hardware used to keep the bindings intact are too short, causing the binding to separate from the shoe. This poses a fall hazard to consumers.
firm: Trak Inc., doing business as Karhu Inc., of Burlington, Vt.
distribution: Skiboards.com web site, LL Bean, Cabela's, Erehwon Mountain Outfitters, and Vail Bicycle stores sold these snowshoes nationwide, during November 2002, for about $250.
hazards: Screws and other hardware used to keep the bindings intact are too short, causing the binding to separate from the shoe. This poses a fall hazard to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should immediately stop using these snowshoes and return them to the store where purchased for a free repair kit.
injuries: CPSC and Trak Inc. are not aware of any injuries involving these bindings. This recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.

title: CPSC, Thomas & Betts Announce Recall of Emergency Exit Signs
reason: The emergency exit signs have an internal electrical component that could overheat and fail, when connected to 277-volt electrical systems, and melt the enclosure, posing a fire hazard.
distribution: The emergency exit signs were sold nationwide by electrical wholesalers and distributors for between $75 and $80.
hazards: The emergency exit signs have an internal electrical component that could overheat and fail, when connected to 277-volt electrical systems, and melt the enclosure, posing a fire hazard.
remedies: Building managers with recalled emergency exit signs should contact Thomas & Betts to request a free repair kit.
injuries: There have been 19 reports of these emergency exit signs overheating and smoking or causing melted or damaged enclosures. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Eton America Announce Recall of Youth All-Terrain Vehicles (ATVs)
reason: The ATV contains a remote shutoff switch that shuts the ATV off. For the remote shutoff switch to work, the receiver switch on the ATV must be in the on position. It was possible for the ATV to be started with the receiver switch in the off position. The ATV could not be shutoff with the remote switch, should the rider start to act in an unsafe manner. This could cause serious bodily harm.
distribution: Dealerships nationwide sold these ATVs, from August 2002 through January 2003, for $1500.
hazards: The ATV contains a remote shutoff switch that shuts the ATV off. For the remote shutoff switch to work, the receiver switch on the ATV must be in the on position. It was possible for the ATV to be started with the receiver switch in the off position. The ATV could not be shutoff with the remote switch, should the rider start to act in an unsafe manner. This could cause serious bodily harm.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these ATVs immediately and contact their local dealer to schedule an appointment for their ATV to be repaired. Owners of these ATVs have been notified.

title: CPSC, Zenith Announce Recall to Repair Large-Screen, Analog Projection Televisions
reason: A tear in a gasket can cause coolant fluid to leak from the picture tube assembly. This can cause smoking, charring, and electrical arcing inside of the television, posing a fire hazard to consumers.
firm: Zenith Electronics Corp., of Lincolnshire, Ill.
distribution: Major appliance and department stores nationwide sold these televisions, from about April 1995 through April 1999, for between $1,200 and $2,800.
hazards: A tear in a gasket can cause coolant fluid to leak from the picture tube assembly. This can cause smoking, charring, and electrical arcing inside of the television, posing a fire hazard to consumers.
remedies: Consumers who have one of these televisions should immediately contact Zenith to arrange for a free inspection and repair.
injuries: Since 1998, Zenith has received 45 reports of incidents involving coolant leakage, causing smoking or charring with the televisions, including four cases where minor property damage occurred outside of the unit. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Cooper Lighting Warn About 500-Watt Halogen Bulbs
reason: These 500-watt light bulbs generate very high temperatures, compared to incandescent and lower wattage halogen bulbs and can start a fire, if they come in contact with curtains, clothes or other flammable material. These bulbs are intended for use in outdoor work lights and flood lamps. To meet the current Underwriters Laboratories standard, halogen torchiere floor lamps must be equipped with a protective glass or wire guard and have a halogen bulb that is 300 watts or less.
firm: Cooper Lighting Inc., of Peachtree City, Ga.
distribution: Wal-Mart, Lowe's and smaller retail outlets nationwide sold these 500-watt halogen bulbs, between January 1999 and October 2002, for about $4.
hazards: These 500-watt light bulbs generate very high temperatures, compared to incandescent and lower wattage halogen bulbs and can start a fire, if they come in contact with curtains, clothes or other flammable material. These bulbs are intended for use in outdoor work lights and flood lamps. To meet the current Underwriters Laboratories standard, halogen torchiere floor lamps must be equipped with a protective glass or wire guard and have a halogen bulb that is 300 watts or less.
remedies: Cooper has asked retailers to add the label to bulb packaging currently on store shelves and new 500-watt halogen bulbs will contain the label. Consumers currently using these 500-watt bulbs in a torchiere or indoor residential fixture should remove them immediately. Consumers can continue to use the 500-watt halogen bulbs in work lights, flood lamps, and similar outdoor fixtures.
injuries: While Cooper has not received any reports of fires or injuries, the CPSC is aware of at least 290 fires and 25 deaths since 1992, involving halogen torchiere floor lamps.

title: CPSC, Xerox International Partners Announce Retrofit of Network Laser Printers
product: Xerox, Hitachi, and GCC brand laser printers
reason: Arcing may cause the fuser assembly to overheat, posing a fire hazard.
distribution: Xerox Engineering Systems, Hitachi Printing Solutions America and GCC Technologies sold the printers nationwide for prices ranging from $1,599 to $6,999.
hazards: Arcing may cause the fuser assembly to overheat, posing a fire hazard.
remedies: Users should (1) switch off the printer power when unattended; (2) ensure that the "power save" mode is enabled; and (3) contact their commercial distributor for information on obtaining a free retrofit.
injuries: There have been three reports of overheating, causing minor property damage. No injuries have been reported.

title: CPSC, Tim Hortons Announce Recall of Travel Mugs
product: Tim Hortons 15-ounce stainless steel travel mugs
reason: The lids on some of the mugs can detach, allowing hot liquid to leak, posing a burn hazard to consumers.
distribution: Tim Hortons stores in New York, Michigan, Ohio, West Virginia, Kentucky, Maine and Canada sold the mugs, from October 2002 through January 2003, for about $15
hazards: The lids on some of the mugs can detach, allowing hot liquid to leak, posing a burn hazard to consumers.
remedies: Consumers should stop using these mugs immediately and return the old lids to a Tim Hortons store for a replacement lid as of February 1, 2003. Consumers will also receive a full refund if they return their mug and lid to a Tim Hortons store.
injuries: Tim Hortons has received 14 reports of the lids detaching while mugs were filled with hot liquid. One consumer reported hot liquid spilling onto his hand and chest.

title: CPSC Announces Recall of Baseline Design Beanbag Chairs
reason: Some of these beanbag chairs have zippers that can be opened, allowing access to the polystyrene beads inside the chairs. This poses a suffocation hazard to young children who can unzip the chair and inhale the small beads.
firm: Baseline Design, of Linwood, Pa.
distribution: Wal-Mart stores located in the Northeast U.S. sold the beanbag chairs, from September 1999 through December 1999, for about $30.
hazards: Some of these beanbag chairs have zippers that can be opened, allowing access to the polystyrene beads inside the chairs. This poses a suffocation hazard to young children who can unzip the chair and inhale the small beads.
remedies: Consumers should check if they can unzip their Baseline Design beanbag chairs. If the zippers can be unzipped freely, Baseline Design will provide owners with a free replacement beanbag chair with zippers that do not open. Consumers should be sure young children cannot use the chairs if the zipper can be opened freely and should be sure children are not exposed to the beads inside the chair.
injuries: Baseline Design is aware of three incidents, in which the chairs were unzipped freely. Two of the incidents involved young children who were able to open the beanbag chair zippers and handle the small polystyrene beads, including one child who received medical attention after inhaling the beads.

title: CPSC, Walt Disney Parks and Resorts Announce Recall of Woody Dolls
reason: The Woody doll's clothing has buttons that can detach, posing a choking hazard for young children.

hazards: The Woody doll's clothing has buttons that can detach, posing a choking hazard for young children.
remedies: Consumers should immediately take the doll away from children and contact Walt Disney Parks and Resorts to receive a full refund.
injuries: Walt Disney Parks and Resorts has received one report of a child removing a button from the Woody doll. No injuries have been reported.

reason: It is a potential choking hazard to young children.

hazards: It is a potential choking hazard to young children.
remedies: Consumers should immediately take the teething rings away from children and contact Magic Cabin for a full refund and a $15 gift certificate. Known purchasers were sent direct mail notification of this recall.

title: CPSC, Hufco-Delaware Company and Evenflo Company Inc. Announce Recall to Repair Gerry® and Evenflo® Portable Wood Cribs
reason: If the hardware used to assemble the crib is not tight, the mattress support platform and mattress can fall to the floor. This poses a risk of injury to young children in the crib.

injuries: There have been 41 reports of mattresses falling through portable wood cribs. Of these incidents, 17 children suffered bumps, bruises or scratches.

title: CPSC, Polaris Industries Announce Recall of ATVs
reason: The mounting bolts on the front brake calipers were not tightened to the specified torque value. This may cause the bolts to loosen or fall out during operation, resulting in brake failure. This could result in severe injury or death.

distribution: Polaris dealers sold these ATVs nationwide, from November through December 2002, for between $6,000 and $6,300.
hazards: The mounting bolts on the front brake calipers were not tightened to the specified torque value. This may cause the bolts to loosen or fall out during operation, resulting in brake failure. This could result in severe injury or death.
remedies: Consumers should contact their Polaris dealer to schedule an appointment. The dealer will apply the correct torque to the front brake caliper retaining bolts.

reason: The nose of the stuffed bear can be pulled or twisted off, posing a choking hazard to a young child.

reason: The pans can explode or separate when preheated, used on high heat, or used for frying, which can pose a serious burn hazard from hot oil or food contents spilling onto consumers.

hazards: The pans can explode or separate when preheated, used on high heat, or used for frying, which can pose a serious burn hazard from hot oil or food contents spilling onto consumers.

injuries: Innova has received 16 reports of these frying pans exploding, including two consumers who received burns from hot oil and eight reports of property damage.

title: CPSC, American Power Conversion Corp. Announce Recall of Back-Up Power Supply Systems
product: Back-UPS CS350 and Back-UPS CS 500 Back-up Power Supply devices
reason: The power supply device can fail, causing the unit to overheat, which may pose a fire hazard to consumers.

title: CPSC, Pace Products Inc. Announce Recall of Children's Soap Making Kits
